official_primary_status.title: Multi-LLM Systems Exhibit Robust Semantic Collapse

independent_retrieval.method: official byte-range responses reassembled in order

method.finding: Closed-loop, text-only multi-LLM simulations separate lexical diversity, within-run semantic displacement, and aligned cross-run diversity; three primary models use three 1000-round triadic runs each, with other disclosed interventions generally evaluated over 200 rounds and three runs per condition.

locators: Results: Semantic Collapse in Extended Open-Ended Simulations
Results: Diagnosing Mechanisms of Semantic Collapse
evaluation.finding: The paper evaluates twelve disclosed intervention categories and reports no positive statistically significant semantic-diversity improvement across 62 baseline comparisons after Bonferroni correction.

limitations_and_counterevidence.finding: The regression does not warrant mechanistic or causal interpretation, and the recursive-channel analogies are heuristic guides rather than established empirical properties.

non_proof_boundary: Does not prove that every multi-agent architecture collapses.
Does not cover systems with sustained external evidence, tools, humans, or environment renewal.
Does not establish recursive-channel dynamics as a causal mechanism.
Does not establish the chosen semantic-diversity metrics as universal novelty measures.
